newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market sees wave of fresh inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market sees wave of fresh inquiry.

text.p: The sugar freight market saw a spate of fresh inquiry on Wednesday with Cuban and other Latin American origins once again occupying centre stage, shipbrokers said.

Sugar Exporters quoted for 14,000 tonnes in bags from Maceio to Tema and Lagos for mid-February and Sucre Export for a same-sized bulk cargo from Cuba to Baltic/Mediterranean/Black Sea for the same dates.
Shipbrokers said Commodity Specialists was in the market for 14/15,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Puerto Quetzal or Acajutla to US Gulf/Atlantic for the end of February.
CSR was said to be closely working its recent March order for 23,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to Japan.
Tate & Lyle was thought to have booked tonnage to ship 17,100 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maputo to London for mid-February dates, but details of the rate achieved have yet to emerge.

Cargill was open for 14,700 tonnes of bagged sugar from Denmark to Tunisia, Egypt or syria for mid-February and Jean Lion quoted for 12/17,000 tonnes of bulk raws from Cuba to the Black Sea for the end of the month.
Other orders included Seven Seas, which was in the market for 13/14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Thailand to east Africa/Red Sea for mid-February.
In other news, Iran's Government Trading Corporation (GTC) tendered to buy 14,000 tonnes of white sugar for April delivery.
Permitted origins under the tender terms are the European Union (excluding U.K.), Thailand and Brazil.
Sugar shipments have eased in Brazilian ports, with just 9,572 tonnes expected for loading in Santos, 12,000 tonnes of bagged sugar loading in Maceio and 42,000 tonnes loading in Recife.
